newsitem.title: ITALY: Centre-left candidate leads in Trieste -Abacus.
newsitem.headline: Centre-left candidate leads in Trieste -Abacus.

text.p: Italy's governing centre-left coalition led in a mayoral race in the northeastern Adriatic city of Trieste but its fortunes in the south were mixed, according to a forecast made after two thirds of votes had been counted.
Local coffee roasting magnate Riccardo Illy, the governing Olive Tree's candidate, was in front with 37.7 percent after a first round of voting, the forecast by the Abacus polling institute showed.

The opposition vote was split between far-right National Alliance candidate Sergio Dressi with 22.1 percent of the vote and centre right party Forza Italia's (Go Italy) Adalberto Donaggio who polled 21.8 percent.
The forecast was made for RAI and Mediaset television stations.
Illy will face Dressi in a second round run-off on May 11.

The centre-right Freedom Alliance was ahead in Milan and Turin -- the key contests in elections for mayors and local councils in more than 1,100 towns and cities in the first big test of electoral support since Prime Minister Romano Prodi's coalition won last April's general election.

In Catanzaro, in Italy's deep south, Abacus put centre-right candidate Sergio Abramo in front with 45.9 percent, ahead of the Olive Tree's Fortunato Costantino with 30 percent, after three quarters of votes had been counted.
Further to the south, in Reggio Calabria, Olive Tree candidate Italo Falcomata was forecast by Abacus to win outright in the first round after polling 53.9 percent of the vote.
Freedom Alliance candidate Antonio Monorchio trailed with 40.4 percent.
